title: The Monkey's Paw
author: W. W. Jacobs
note: Sample for testing the interface only. Lines are short stand-ins, not the real adaptation.

characters.name: Narrator
characters.description: Calm, low storyteller voice, older British man, unhurried, a hint of dread.

characters.name: Mr White
characters.description: Elderly British father, cheerful and curious, slightly reedy voice.

characters.name: Mrs White
characters.description: Elderly British mother, warm but sharp, later raw with grief.

characters.name: Herbert
characters.description: Young British man in his twenties, teasing, playful, quick.

characters.name: Sergeant-Major Morris
characters.description: Weathered British soldier, gravelly, guarded, speaks in short sentences.

characters.name: The man from Maw and Meggins
characters.description: Nervous, formal British clerk, hesitant, apologetic.

scenes.title: The parlour
scenes.ambience: wind and rain outside, crackling fire indoors

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [quietly] Outside, the night was cold and wet. Inside, the fire burned bright.

lines.speaker: mr-white
lines.text: Listen to the wind. I hope he still comes tonight.

lines.speaker: herbert
lines.text: [laughing] Father, nobody walks out this far on a night like this.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: [low] It is just a little paw. Dried. Nothing to look at.

lines.speaker: mrs-white
lines.text: [uneasy] Then why do you keep it, Sergeant-Major?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A stranger stood at the gate, as if he could not decide to come in.

lines.speaker: maw-meggins-man
lines.text: [hesitant] I was asked to call. I come from Maw and Meggins.

lines.speaker: mrs-white
lines.text: [whispers] Is it Herbert? Is something wrong with Herbert?
